subject: Acme POC: Access, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme.com>, Jamie Wu <jamie.wu@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC: Access, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Alex / Jamie,

Great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we're all aligned: 

Goal: Validate Redwood Inference can meet Acme's latency (95p < 200ms) and throughput needs (sustained 60 qps for search reranking) while keeping per-request cost within your target.

Success criteria (draft):
- Average inference latency (95th percentile) <= 200ms for 512-token prompts
- Throughput: sustain 60 qps for 30-minute window with <5% error rate
- Accuracy: top-5 rerank precision lift >= 7% on your eval set
- Integration: end-to-end roundtrip from your service to Redwood <= 300ms

Timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): access and credentials provisioned
- Week 1: smoke tests + baseline run with your sample dataset
- Week 2: tuning, batching and quantization recommendations from our side
- Week 3: final eval run and sync to review results

Ownership:
- Redwood: dev_patel (SE) for access & infra; ethan_park (CS) for onboarding + eval tracking
- Acme: Alex (technical lead) and Jamie (product owner)

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm the IP ranges for allowlisting (we recommend adding our ingestion IPs below)
2) Point-of-contact for SSO invitations (Okta admin email)
3) Confirm whether you need production-like dataset or a sampled subset for Week 1

IP allowlist (for initial sandbox): 34.201.15.20/32, 34.201.15.21/32

I've attached a quick POC success-criteria workbook and our short access guide. Dev, can you please provision a sandbox API key for Acme and prepare an Okta invite if they want SSO? Ethan, I'll add you to the eval doc.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: acme-poc-success-criteria.xlsx, redwood-poc-access-instructions.pdf

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Wu <jamie.wu@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC: Access, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks Marissa, this looks good and aligns with internal expectations. A few notes from our side:

- Okta admin for invites: samir.kohli@acme.com (please send SSO invite to that email).
- IP allowlist: we can add the two IPs you listed; also add 18.205.93.0/24 for our analyst bastion.
- For Week 1, we'll start with a sampled dataset (5k queries) — will share S3 location by EOD today.

Question on access: do you provision a single API key scoped to the sandbox project, or do you prefer separate keys per engineer? Security prefers per-engineer keys, but we can start with a shared key if that's faster.

Also, can you confirm if there's an Okta SCIM provisioning option to auto-create users?

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Torres
Principal ML Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC: Access, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks, we'll get everything ready. Quick answers:
- We'll create scoped API keys by default (recommended) — one project-level key for sandbox plus optional per-engineer keys if you want tighter auditability. I'll provision a shared sandbox key right away and can follow up with individual keys.
- Okta: we support SCIM and SAML. If Samir wants SCIM, we'll need their SCIM base URL and an API token (we can provide the schema and a short runbook). If they prefer SAML, we'll send metadata for self-service setup.
- IP allowlist: we'll add 34.201.15.20 and 34.201.15.21 to the sandbox; we can also allow 18.205.93.0/24 as requested for your bastion.

Provisioning plan (eta):
- Today: create sandbox project + shared API key; send key over Secure Note (and create per-engineer keys on request)
- Today: send Okta SAML metadata + SCIM runbook to samir.kohli@acme.com (cc'd if you add him)
- Tomorrow: baseline smoke test with Acme's sample S3 dataset; Ethan will run the eval harness and populate the results in the shared doc

I'm provisioning the key now — expect the Secure Note link in ~30 mins.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-sso-scim-runbook.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC: Access, success criteria, and next steps

Perfect, thanks Alex and Dev. For transparency I've added the timeline to the shared doc and linked the HubSpot deal. Next immediate items:

- Dev: please send the Secure Note with the sandbox API key (mark expiry 30 days) and add instructions for rotating keys.
- Alex / Samir: confirm whether you want SCIM or SAML by EOD Monday so we can schedule the SSO setup in Week 1.
- Ethan: will kick off the baseline run on Monday once the sample S3 path is available.

I'll follow up after the baseline run with an updated success-criteria sheet and the first set of measurements. Excited to get this going.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Related links: HubSpot deal, shared drive, DocuSign for the POC MSSA (if they request it)
